 Judgment

In these two appeals, both the petitioners as well as the B.M.T.C. have challenged the judgment and award dated 07.04.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.733/2015 by the Member, Principal M.A.C.T.,
Bangalore (SCCH-1) ('the Tribunal' for short).
NC: 2023:KHC:40456 2.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 by name Ramakrishna, the deceased, while crossing the road near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk on Kanakapura Main Road on 08.01.2015 at about 08.20 p.m., hit by BMTC bus bearing No.KA-01/FA-733 injuring him.
He died during transit to the hospital.
Petitioners claiming that the deceased was aged 55 years doing Panipuri business and earning Rs.15,000/- per month have sought for grant of compensation of Rs.20 lakhs.

The claim was opposed by the B.M.T.C. on the ground that there is a collusion between the petitioners and the Police in concocting a case of accident, the bus in question was not involved in the accident and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
2 NC: 2023:KHC:40456 4.

On the basis of the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.01.2015 at about 8.20 p.m near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Kanakapura Mail Road, Thalaghattapura within the jurisdiction of Thalaghattapura Police Station on account of rash and negligent driving of the BMTC bus bearing registration No. KA-01-FA-733 by its driver?
2) Whether the petitioner are entitled for compensation ?

If so, how much and from whom?
3) What Order?
5. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, two witnesses are examined as PWs-1 and 2 and eight documents came to be marked as Exs.P1 to P8.
On behalf of the respondent, three witnesses are examined as RW-1 to RW-3 and three documents came to be marked as Exs.R1 to R3.

The Tribunal after hearing both parties by the impugned judgment assessed the compensation of Rs.8,69,000/- and attributed 25% of negligence on NC: 2023:KHC:40456 the part of the deceased and directed the BMTC to deposit 75% of the compensation i.e., Rs.6,51,750/-.

Aggrieved by the same, the BMTC has filed M.F.A.No.5934/2016; pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement,
petitioners have filed M.F.A.No.5819/2016.
6. Heard the arguments of Sri.D.Vijaya Kumar, learned Counsel for the B.M.T.C. and Sri.H.R.Sathyapal Hegde, learned Counsel for the petitioners.

7. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the BMTC that the accident took place at 8.20 p.m.
on 08.01.2015; there were no eyewitnesses to the incident, it is a 'hit and run' case whereas the complaint under Ex.P1 was filed before the Police at 10.15 p.m.; there were several vehicles ply across at the place of accident and it is alleged that some riders of the motor cycles have intercepted the bus in question at about 9.20 p.m. at a distance of one NC: 2023:KHC:40456 kilometer and also it was informed to Kaggalipura Police who retained the bus for about 20 minutes, later after confirming that the bus was not involved in the accident, it was let go.
The bus in question travelled from Kalasipalya Bus Stand towards Kanakapura on that day.
It had departed the Bus Stand at 7.45 p.m., the place of accident is 22 kilometers away, within the city, it is impossible to reach the place of accident within 35 minutes.

7.1. On behalf of the BMTC, the evidence of conductor of the bus, a passenger in the bus has been examined as RW-3, who is the eyewitness and she has categorically stated that the bus was not involved in the accident.
Petitioner No.1/PW-1 is not an eyewitness to the accident.
But in the evidence, she claims that she saw the bus hitting against her husband and there is no such reference in the Police investigating papers.

Hence, the evidence placed by the petitioners is unreliable and the cogent evidence NC: 2023:KHC:40456 placed on behalf of the BMTC is not accepted by the The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
3 Tribunal.
7.2.
He further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded compensation under conventional heads disproportionately, which needs modification.

It is further contended that the rate of interest awarded at 9% per annum is exorbitant and no Banks will grant rate of interest at 9% and he sought for reduction of rate of interest in case award is sustained and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that soon after causing the accident,
driver did not stop the vehicle at the spot.
There are eyewitnesses to the incident.

The petitioners were sitting in the auto rickshaw nearby the Panipuri shop run by the deceased; they have seen the accident; some motorists present at the NC: 2023:KHC:40456 spot chased the bus, which was going ahead, intercepted and the bus was stopped.
Within two hours of the accident, complaint was lodged to the Police with specific reference to the bus number.

If really the petitioners want to falsely implicate the bus in question, on the same road, several BMTC buses were plying and they could have mentioned any bus and they could have stopped any one of the BMTC buses and attributed negligence.
Merely because the driver of the bus did not stop the bus does not mean that there was no accident.
On the allegation of 'hit and run' case, the driver has been prosecuted under Section 134 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The prosecution of the driver of the BMTC bus is admitted.
The BMTC did not challenge either the FIR or the charge sheet.
Without challenging the same, it has no right to question the legality of the evidence relied upon by the petitioners.
At one breath, BMTC claims that there was no accident and another breath, it allows the driver to stand for NC: 2023:KHC:40456 criminal trial for causing the accident in question.
The Tribunal evaluated the evidence of both sides and came to the right conclusion that there was an accident involving the bus in question and thereby the award is passed.

8.1. It is further contended that in the year 2015, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.9,000/- whereas, the Tribunal has taken the income of Rs.7,000/- which is meager; the deceased was doing Panipuri business and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and submitted that income ought to have been taken not less than Rs.10,000/- and sought for enhancement of the compensation.
9. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
It is the petitioners, who pleaded that there was an accident involving the bus in question.

To substantiate the same, on record, we have the evidence of petitioner No.1 as PW-1, Police records such as, Ex.P1/FIR, Ex.P2/charge sheet, Ex.P3/IMV report, Ex.P4/sketch, Ex.P5/mahazar and Ex.P6/inquest report.
The Police investigating papers point out that there was an accident as pleaded by the petitioners in the claim petition.

The driver of the bus has been prosecuted in Crime The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
4 No.10/2015 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC and Sections 134(A)
and (B) and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Nowhere in the evidence, it is pleaded or averred or suggested to the petitioners' witnesses that the BMTC has questioned the prosecution of its driver.

When the driver and the BMTC both have not challenged the criminal prosecution, the point that - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 arises for consideration is, whether there is an independent evidence to accept the contention of the petitioner in addition to the criminal prosecution of the driver.
11. PW-1 on oath reiterates the accident.
She has been cross-examined.

Except formal denial,
nothing is elicited from her mouth.
Though she claims that she saw the accident, there is no reference either in the criminal prosecution or in the charge sheet that she is an eyewitness.
Even if her evidence is excluded from the array of evidence, PW- 2/Smt.Rekha, the sister-in-law of petitioner No.1 has sworn to as an eyewitness before the Court.

She has specifically stated in her evidence by way of affidavit that at the time of accident, she, her husband Narayan and the first petitioner Lakshmamma were sitting in the auto opposite to Indian Oil Petrol Bunk.
They were waiting for the arrival of the deceased after finishing his business to - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 go back home.
While the deceased was crossing the road, the bus in question had caused the accident.
Though she has been cross-
examined, nothing has been elicited to discredit that she is not an eyewitness to the accident.
To support her contention, she has been cited as an eyewitness to the accident as CW-5 and her husband CW- 4/Narayan as eyewitness in the charge sheet. PW-2
may be a relative of the petitioners, but she has given statement before the Police about her presence at the place of accident.
12. To rebut the evidence of the petitioners, the driver of the bus has entered into witness box as RW-1/S.Prakash and conductor of the bus as RW- 2/D.C.Nagaraj.
Both reiterate non-involvement of the bus in question.
The driver admits that he has been charge sheeted and he is facing the criminal trial.
He has not challenged either the FIR or charge sheet.

From the evidence of driver and conductor,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 we can make out that at the relevant point of time, bus in question has passed through the place of accident.

There is no material on record to show that either driver or the conductor reporting the said incident of intercepting of bus by the motorists and also the retention of the bus at Kaggalipura Police Station to their superiors.

The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
5 13.
The star witness to the BMTC is RW- 3/Smt.Sunitha.
To show that she was one of the passengers of the bus, the BMTC has relied upon Ex.R3/tickets.
There are two tickets of denomination of 10 and one ticket of denomination of 6.
Ex.R2, the Conductor's trip sheet indicates mentioning of ticket numbers.
She has asserted in the witness box on oath that she was travelling from City Bus Stand to Vadayarahalli in the said BMTC bus.
The said bus left the City Market at 7.45 p.m., it reached her destination at 10.10 p.m., bus was loaded with full passengers.
According to her, two persons came in - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 motor cycle and stopped the bus at Kuppireddy Kere Bus stand stating that the bus caused the accident near NICE road.
When the driver denied it, they allowed the driver to proceed further.
At Pattereddypalya, the Kaggalipura Police came and stopped the bus and it was retained there for about 20 minutes and after confirming that the bus was not involved in the accident, it was let free.
During the course of cross-examination, she has denied that she was not at all a passenger of the bus.
The bus was fully loaded with 60 to 70 passengers.
There are standing passengers also in the bus.
Her evidence did not point out where she was sitting in the bus, whether she was having a vision of the road on the front and either side of the bus.

What made her to come before the Court to give evidence on behalf of the BMTC, how BMTC knew that she is a passenger in the bus at the relevant point of time and she retaining the bus ticket and producing it before the Tribunal on 29.02.2016 i.e., after 13 - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 months of the accident
is not explained.
Hence, even if she is accepted as a passenger of the bus, she cannot be an eyewitness.
14. Adverting to the argument of the learned Counsel for BMTC that the bus left the K.R.Market at 7.45 p.m., the accident took place at 8.20 p.m.
The distance between the K.R.Market and the place of accident is around 22 kilometers.
Bus has traveled 35 kilometers; in a traffic free movement, it is possible that one can reach the place of accident within 35 minutes of their departure.

Admittedly,
the bus has traveled on the road, soon after the accident, the bus was intercepted by the motorists,
when the bus reached near Kaggalipura, it was stopped by the Kaggalipura Police with a specific enquiry about involvement of the bus in the accident.

If really the parties want to implicate this bus,
they could have even implicated the other buses at the spot itself.
It is pertinent to note that Bangalore- Kanakapura Road is a busy road where a lot of BMTC buses are being plied.
I have carefully examined the reasons recorded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has taken all relevant factors into consideration that the bus can pass through the place of accident by 8.30 p.m. and accident has been witnessed by the eyewitnesses, driver of the bus did not stop the The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
6 bus at the spot, prosecution of the driver has not been challenged either by the dr0iver or the BMTC.

Hence, the evidence on record probabalizes that the bus in question is involved in the accident and the Tribunal has correctly recorded that the accident took place due to involvement of the bus in question.
I am not persuaded by the evidence and argument of the BMTC to accept the defence.

16. Adverting to the award of compensation under conventional heads is exorbitant as argued by - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 the BMTC, so also the interest at 9% per annum, award of compensation under conventional heads has been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1, so also the selection of multiplier in Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2.

sentences.text:
By applying the said principles,
the compensation has to be determined.

17. As regards rate of interest at 9% is concerned, the Division Bench of this Court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest, it reads thus:
"52.Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted. . . . . . . . .
. . "

18. In view of the settled principles, it is reasonable to award interest at 6% p.a. instead of 9%.
19.
The material on record did point out that the deceased was doing Panipuri business, which cannot be a permanent employment earning regular source of income.
Hence, the principle of notional income has to be applied.
In the year 2015, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.9,000/-, whereas, the Tribunal taken the income at Rs.7,000/-.
Hence, the income assessed - 19 - The Managing Director vs Smt. Lakshmamma on 10 November, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18840292/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:40456 by the Tribunal is on the lower side and it ought to have been taken at Rs.9,000/-.

By applying the above principles, if the compensation is assessed, the notional income of the deceased will be Rs.9,000/- + Rs.1,350/- (15% future prospects) = Rs.10,350/- - Rs.3,450/-
(1/3rd) = Rs.6,900/- x 12 x 11 = Rs.9,10,800/- towards loss of dependency.
Towards conventional heads, the deceased left behind his wife and son.
Hence, loss of consortium to wife and loss of love and affection to her son at Rs.40,000/- each has to be assessed.
Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is assessed.

In all, compensation comes to Rs.10,20,800/-.
20.
The Tribunal has recorded its finding that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
The accident took place at 8.20 p.m., it was night.

The relatives of the deceased were waiting for him in the auto rickshaw to go back home - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 in a hurry towards whom he rushed himself and based on the evidence, the Tribunal attributed 25% of contributory negligence against the deceased.
Hence, I do not find any reason in the ground urged by the petitioners.

Hence, the contributory negligence of 25%
determined by the Tribunal is maintained.
If that is so, out of total compensation of Rs.10,20,800/-

,
the petitioners are entitled to 75%, which comes to Rs.7,65,600/-.
21.
In view of the law laid down in Ms.Joyeeta Bose's case (supra), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% is not the prevailing Bank rate of interest and as rightly contended by the BMTC,
it ought to have been reduced to 6%, which is the reasonable sum that the petitioners are entitled to.
In a case of this nature, it shall not be a bonanza nor a peanut for the petitioners, but at the same time, it shall not be a penalty for the BMTC.
Hence, the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to is - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC:40456 Rs.7,65,600/- as against Rs.6,51,750/- assessed by the Tribunal with interest @ 6% per annum.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment needs modification.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part;

(v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
